sanskrit: bhīmasenaḥ kurūn sarvān putrāṃś ca tava māriṣa sahānīkān mahābāhur eka evābhyavārayat
english: Bhīmasena of the mighty arms, O honored one, single-handedly held back all the Kurus and your sons together with their troops.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī ca tataḥ karṇaṃ vicarantam abhītavat bhīṣmahantā mahārāja vārayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, slayer of Bhīṣma, O great king, checked with his arrows Karṇa, who was ranging fearlessly over the field.

sanskrit: pratirabdhas tataḥ karṇo roṣāt prasphuritādharaḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ tribhir bāṇair bhruvor madhye vyatāḍayat
english: Thus opposed, Karṇa, his lips quivering with rage, struck Śikhaṇḍin with three arrows between the brows.

sanskrit: dhārayaṃs tu sa tān bāṇāñ śikhaṇḍī bahv aśobhata rājataḥ parvato yadvat tribhiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ samanvitaḥ
english: Bearing those arrows, Śikhaṇḍin shone in great splendor, like a silver mountain crowned with three peaks.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ sūtaputreṇa saṃyuge karṇaṃ vivyādha samare navatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: That mighty archer, sorely wounded by the sūta's son in the encounter, pierced Karṇa in battle with ninety sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo hayān hatvā sārathiṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ unmamātha dhvajaṃ cāsya kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ
english: Karṇa, that great chariot-warrior, slew his horses and his charioteer with three arrows, and tore down his banner with a razor-edged shaft.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu tato yānād avaplutya mahārathaḥ śaktiṃ cikṣepa karṇāya saṃkruddhaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Then that great chariot-warrior, scorcher of foes, leaping down from his car of slain horses, in fury hurled a spear at Karṇa.

sanskrit: tāṃ chittvā samare karṇas tribhir bhārata sāyakaiḥ śikhaṇḍinam athāvidhyan navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Cleaving that spear in battle with three arrows, O Bhārata, Karṇa then pierced Śikhaṇḍin with nine sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: karṇacāpacyutān bāṇān varjayaṃs tu narottamaḥ apayātas tatas tūrṇaṃ śikhaṇḍī jayatāṃ varaḥ
english: Warding off the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, that best of men, Śikhaṇḍin, foremost of the victorious, then swiftly withdrew.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja pāṇḍusainyāny aśātayat tūlarāśiṃ samāsādya yathā vāyur mahājavaḥ
english: Then Karṇa, O great king, scattered the Pāṇḍava forces, as a swift-rushing wind falls upon a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja tava putreṇa pīḍitaḥ duḥśāsanaṃ tribhir bāṇair abhyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, hard pressed by your son, pierced Duḥśāsana with three arrows in the breast.

sanskrit: tasya duḥśāsano bāhuṃ savyaṃ vivyādha māriṣa śitena rukmapuṅkhena bhallena nataparvaṇā
english: Duḥśāsana in turn pierced his left arm, O honored one, with a sharp, gold-feathered, broad-headed arrow of smooth joints.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu nirviddhaḥ śaraṃ ghoram amarṣaṇaḥ duḥśāsanāya saṃkruddhaḥ preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Pierced through, the unforgiving Dhṛṣṭadyumna, enraged, sped a dreadful arrow at Duḥśāsana, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ mahāvegaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnasamīritam śaraiś ciccheda putras te tribhir eva viśāṃ pate
english: As that arrow loosed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna sped toward him with great force, your son cut it apart with three shafts, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: athāparaiḥ saptadaśair bhallaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ samāsādya bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: Then, closing in, he tormented Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the arms and chest with seventeen more broad-headed, gold-adorned arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pārṣataḥ kruddho dhanuś ciccheda māriṣa kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: Then that son of Pṛṣata in fury cut his bow apart, O honored one, with a keen-edged razor-shaft, whereupon the people raised a great shout.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya putras te bharatarṣabha dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ śaravrātaiḥ samantāt paryavārayat
english: Then, taking up another bow, your son, O bull of the Bharatas, hemmed in Dhṛṣṭadyumna on every side with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tava putrasya te dṛṣṭvā vikramaṃ taṃ mahātmanaḥ vyahasanta raṇe yodhāḥ siddhāś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: Beholding the prowess of your high-souled son, the warriors in the field, the Siddhas, and the hosts of Apsarases broke into joyous acclaim.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha ghoraṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ kāle ghorarūpaṃ paraṃtapa
english: Then there raged between your men and the foe a battle dreadful and terrible of aspect, as though it were the appointed hour of doom for all living things, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ vṛṣasenas tu viddhvā pañcabhir āyasaiḥ pituḥ samīpe tiṣṭhantaṃ tribhir anyair avidhyata
english: Vṛṣasena, having pierced Nakula with five iron arrows, struck him again with three others as he stood near his father.

sanskrit: nakulas tu tataḥ kruddho vṛṣasenaṃ smayann iva nārācena sutīkṣṇena vivyādha hṛdaye dṛḍham
english: Then Nakula, enraged, as if with a smile, pierced Vṛṣasena deep in the heart with a keen iron shaft.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā śatruṇā śatrukarśanaḥ śatruṃ vivyādha viṃśatyā sa ca taṃ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Sorely wounded by his powerful foe, that harasser of enemies pierced his foe with twenty arrows, and the other struck him with five.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa tāv ubhau puruṣarṣabhau anyonyam ācchādayatām athābhajyata vāhinī
english: Then those two bulls among men covered each other with a thousand arrows, and the host was broken asunder.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pradrutāṃ senāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya sūtajaḥ nivārayām āsa balād anupatya viśāṃ pate nivṛtte tu tataḥ karṇe nakulaḥ kauravān yayau
english: Seeing Dhṛtarāṣṭra's army in flight, the sūta's son pursued and forcibly rallied it, O lord of peoples; and when Karṇa had thus turned away, Nakula advanced against the Kauravas.

sanskrit: karṇaputras tu samare hitvā nakulam eva tu jugopa cakraṃ tvaritaṃ rādheyasyaiva māriṣa
english: And Karṇa's son, leaving Nakula in the battle, swiftly hastened to guard the wheel of Rādheya's chariot, O honored one.

sanskrit: ulūkas tu raṇe kruddhaḥ sahadevena vāritaḥ tasyāśvāṃś caturo hatvā sahadevaḥ pratāpavān sārathiṃ preṣayām āsa yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Ulūka, enraged in battle, was checked by Sahadeva; and the valiant Sahadeva, having slain his four horses, dispatched his charioteer to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: ulūkas tu tato yānād avaplutya viśāṃ pate trigartānāṃ balaṃ pūrṇaṃ jagāma pitṛnandanaḥ
english: Then Ulūka, that delight of his father, leaping down from his car, O lord of peoples, made his way to the full strength of the Trigartas.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ śakuniṃ viddhvā viṃśatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ dhvajaṃ ciccheda bhallena saubalasya hasann iva
english: Sātyaki, having pierced Śakuni with twenty sharpened arrows, cut down the banner of Subala's son with a broad-headed shaft, as if in sport.

sanskrit: saubalas tasya samare kruddho rājan pratāpavān vidārya kavacaṃ bhūyo dhvajaṃ ciccheda kāñcanam
english: Subala's son, valiant and enraged in that battle, O king, rent his armor and in turn cut down his golden banner.

sanskrit: athainaṃ niśitair bāṇaiḥ sātyakiḥ pratyavidhyata sārathiṃ ca mahārāja tribhir eva samārdayat athāsya vāhāṃs tvaritaḥ śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Then Sātyaki struck him back with sharpened arrows and tormented his charioteer, O great king, with three shafts; and swiftly with his arrows he sent his horses to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tato 'vaplutya sahasā śakunir bharatarṣabha āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇam ulūkasya mahārathaḥ apovāhātha śīghraṃ sa śaineyād yuddhaśālinaḥ
english: Then Śakuni, that great chariot-warrior, leaping down at once, O bull of the Bharatas, swiftly mounted Ulūka's car and was quickly borne away from the battle-loving grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu raṇe rājaṃs tāvakānām anīkinīm abhidudrāva vegena tato 'nīkam abhidyata
english: Then Sātyaki in the battle, O king, rushed with speed upon the host of your men, and thereupon the array was broken.

sanskrit: śaineyaśaranunnaṃ tu tataḥ sainyaṃ viśāṃ pate bheje daśa diśas tūrṇaṃ nyapatac ca gatāsuvat
english: Driven by the arrows of Śini's grandson, the army, O lord of peoples, swiftly fled in all ten directions and fell as if its life had departed.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tava suto vārayām āsa saṃyuge taṃ tu bhīmo muhūrtena vyaśvasūtarathadhvajam cakre lokeśvaraṃ tatra tenātuṣyanta cāraṇāḥ
english: Your son withstood Bhīmasena in the encounter; but Bhīma in a moment stripped that lord of the realm of horses, charioteer, car, and banner, whereat the Cāraṇas were well pleased.

sanskrit: tato 'pāyān nṛpas tatra bhīmasenasya gocarāt kurusainyaṃ tataḥ sarvaṃ bhīmasenam upādravat tatra rāvo mahān āsīd bhīmam ekaṃ jighāṃsatām
english: Then the king withdrew there from the range of Bhīmasena; and thereupon the whole Kuru army rushed upon Bhīmasena, and a great uproar arose among those eager to slay Bhīma alone.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyuḥ kṛpaṃ viddhvā dhanur asyāśu cicchide athānyad dhanur ādāya kṛpaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Yudhāmanyu, having pierced Kṛpa, swiftly cut his bow apart; then Kṛpa, foremost of weapon-bearers, took up another bow.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyor dhvajaṃ sūtaṃ chatraṃ cāpātayat kṣitau tato 'pāyād rathenaiva yudhāmanyur mahārathaḥ
english: He brought down to the earth Yudhāmanyu's banner, his charioteer, and his parasol; then Yudhāmanyu, that great chariot-warrior, withdrew upon his car.

sanskrit: uttamaujās tu hārdikyaṃ śarair bhīmaparākramam chādayām āsa sahasā megho vṛṣṭyā yathācalam
english: And Uttamaujas at once covered with arrows the son of Hṛdika, of terrible prowess, as a cloud covers a mountain with its rain.

sanskrit: tad yuddhaṃ sumahac cāsīd ghorarūpaṃ paraṃtapa yādṛśaṃ na mayā yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: That battle was vast and terrible of aspect, O scorcher of foes, such a battle as I had never before beheld, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tato rājann uttamaujasam āhave hṛdi vivyādha sa tadā rathopastha upāviśat
english: Then Kṛtavarman, O king, pierced Uttamaujas in the heart in that combat, and he thereupon sank down on the floor of his car.

sanskrit: sārathis tam apovāha rathena rathināṃ varam tatas tu satvaraṃ rājan pāṇḍusainyam upādravat
english: His charioteer bore that best of car-warriors away upon his chariot; and then in haste, O king, Kṛtavarman fell upon the Pāṇḍava host.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca drauṇis tu rathavaṃśena mahatā parivāritaḥ āpatat sahasā rājan yatra rājā vyavasthitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Droṇa's son, surrounded by a great array of chariots, charged suddenly, O king, to where the king was stationed.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā śūraḥ śaurisahāyavān dadhāra sahasā pārtho veleva makarālayam
english: As he charged in suddenly, the hero Pārtha, with Śauri at his side, at once held him back, as the shore holds back the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān arjunaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca chādayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then, enraged, O great king, the valiant son of Droṇa covered Arjuna and Vāsudeva with his arrows.

sanskrit: avacchannau tataḥ kṛṣṇau dṛṣṭvā tatra mahārathāḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā praikṣanta kuravas tadā
english: Seeing the two Kṛṣṇas thus shrouded, the great chariot-warriors of the Kurus, struck with the utmost wonder, gazed on then.

sanskrit: arjunas tu tato divyam astraṃ cakre hasann iva tad astraṃ brāhmaṇo yuddhe vārayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Arjuna, as if with a smile, brought forth a celestial weapon; but the brāhmaṇa warded off that weapon in the fight, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yad yad dhi vyākṣipad yuddhe pāṇḍavo 'straṃ jighāṃsayā tat tad astraṃ maheṣvāso droṇaputro vyaśātayat
english: Whatever weapon the Pāṇḍava launched in battle, eager to slay, that very weapon the mighty archer, Droṇa's son, beat down.

sanskrit: astrayuddhe tato rājan vartamāne bhayāvahe apaśyāma raṇe drauṇiṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: As the dreadful combat of weapons went on, O king, we beheld Droṇa's son in the battle like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: sa diśo vidiśaś caiva chādayitvā vijihmagaiḥ vāsudevaṃ tribhir bāṇair avidhyad dakṣiṇe bhuje
english: Having veiled all the quarters and the intermediate quarters with his crooked-flying shafts, he pierced Vāsudeva with three arrows in the right arm.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno hayān hatvā sarvāṃs tasya mahātmanaḥ cakāra samare bhūmiṃ śoṇitaughataraṅgiṇīm
english: Then Arjuna, having slain all the horses of that high-souled one, made the ground of the battle a river coursing with streams of blood.

sanskrit: nihatā rathinaḥ petuḥ pārthacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ hayāś ca paryadhāvanta muktayoktrās tatas tataḥ
english: Slain by the arrows loosed from Pārtha's bow, the car-warriors fell, and the horses, their harness loosed, ran hither and thither.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā karma pārthasya drauṇir āhavaśobhinaḥ avākirad raṇe kṛṣṇaṃ samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Seeing that deed of Pārtha, the splendid in battle, Droṇa's son covered Kṛṣṇa on every side with sharpened arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ mahārāja drauṇir āyamya patriṇā vakṣodeśe samāsādya tāḍayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Then, O great king, Droṇa's son, drawing back a feathered shaft, reached Arjuna and struck him in the region of the breast in that encounter.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho raṇe tena droṇaputreṇa bhārata ādatta parighaṃ ghoraṃ drauṇeś cainam avākṣipat
english: Sorely wounded in the battle by Droṇa's son, O Bhārata, he took up a dreadful iron club and hurled it at Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ parighaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam drauṇiś ciccheda sahasā tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: That iron club, adorned with gold, as it hurtled toward him, Droṇa's son at once cut apart, whereupon the people raised a shout.

sanskrit: so 'nekadhāpatad bhūmau bhāradvājasya sāyakaiḥ viśīrṇaḥ parvato rājan yathā syān mātariśvanā
english: Shattered in many pieces by the arrows of Bharadvāja's grandson, it fell to the earth, O king, like a mountain riven by the wind.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno raṇe drauṇiṃ vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apāharat
english: Then Arjuna in the battle pierced Droṇa's son with ten arrows and with a broad-headed shaft swept his charioteer from the chariot-seat.

sanskrit: sa saṃgṛhya svayaṃ vāhān kṛṣṇau prācchādayac charaiḥ tatrādbhutam apaśyāma drauṇer āśu parākramam
english: Taking the reins of his horses himself, he covered the two Kṛṣṇas with his arrows; therein we beheld the wondrous swiftness of Droṇa's son's prowess.

sanskrit: ayacchat turagān yac ca phalgunaṃ cāpy ayodhayat tad asya samare rājan sarve yodhā apūjayan
english: That he held the horses in check and yet did battle with Phalguna—for that, O king, all the warriors in the field honored him.

sanskrit: yadā tv agrasyata raṇe droṇaputreṇa phalgunaḥ tato raśmīn rathāśvānāṃ kṣurapraiś cicchide jayaḥ
english: But when Phalguna was being overborne in battle by Droṇa's son, then Jaya cut apart the reins of his chariot-horses with razor-edged shafts.

sanskrit: prādravaṃs turagās te tu śaravegaprabādhitāḥ tato 'bhūn ninado bhūyas tava sainyasya bhārata
english: Those horses, harried by the force of the arrows, bolted away, and thereupon a great clamor again arose in your army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā tava sainyam upādravan samantān niśitān bāṇān vimuñcanto jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory, fell upon your army, loosing sharpened arrows on every side, eager for triumph.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavais tu mahārāja dhārtarāṣṭrī mahācamūḥ punaḥ punar atho vīrair abhajyata jayoddhataiḥ
english: By the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, those heroes flushed with victory, the great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons was broken again and again.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ te mahārāja putrāṇāṃ citrayodhinām śakuneḥ saubaleyasya karṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Even before the eyes, O great king, of your sons skilled in varied modes of warfare, of Śakuni the son of Subala, and of the high-souled Karṇa,

sanskrit: vāryamāṇā mahāsenā putrais tava janeśvara nāvatiṣṭhata saṃgrāme tāḍyamānā samantataḥ
english: the great army, though rallied by your sons, O lord of men, would not stand its ground in the battle, being smitten on every side.

sanskrit: tato yodhair mahārāja palāyadbhis tatas tataḥ abhavad vyākulaṃ bhītaiḥ putrāṇāṃ te mahad balam
english: Then, O great king, with the warriors fleeing this way and that in terror, the great host of your sons fell into utter confusion.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti satataṃ sūtaputrasya jalpataḥ nāvatiṣṭhata sā senā vadhyamānā mahātmabhiḥ
english: Though the sūta's son cried again and again, "Stand! Stand!", that army, slaughtered by the high-souled ones, would not stand fast.

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ mahārāja pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā dravamāṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: Then, O great king, a great shout was raised by the Pāṇḍavas, flushed with conquest, as they saw the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son fleeing on every side.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ karṇam abravīt praṇayād iva paśya karṇa yathā senā pāṇḍavair arditā bhṛśam
english: Then Duryodhana said to Karṇa, as if in affection: "See, Karṇa, how sorely our army is afflicted by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tvayi tiṣṭhati saṃtrāsāt palāyati samantataḥ etaj jñātvā mahābāho kuru prāptam ariṃdama
english: Even while you stand here, it flees on every side in terror. Knowing this, O mighty-armed subduer of foes, do what the hour demands.

sanskrit: sahasrāṇi ca yodhānāṃ tvām eva puruṣarṣabha krośanti samare vīra drāvyamāṇāni pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Thousands of warriors, O bull among men, O hero, being routed by the Pāṇḍavas in battle, cry out to you alone."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu rādheyo duryodhanavaco mahat madrarājam idaṃ vākyam abravīt sūtanandanaḥ
english: Hearing this weighty speech of Duryodhana, Rādheya, that joy of the sūta, spoke these words to the king of the Madras:

sanskrit: paśya me bhujayor vīryam astrāṇāṃ ca janeśvara adya hanmi raṇe sarvān pāñcālān pāṇḍubhiḥ saha vāhayāśvān naravyāghra bhadreṇaiva janeśvara
english: "Behold the might of my arms and of my weapons, O lord of men. This day I shall slay in battle all the Pāñcālas together with the sons of Pāṇḍu. Drive on the horses with care, O tiger among men, O lord of men."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān pragṛhya vijayaṃ vīro dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ purātanam sajyaṃ kṛtvā mahārāja saṃmṛjya ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, the valiant son of the sūta, that hero, took up Vijaya, his ancient and surpassing bow, strung it, O great king, and stroked it again and again.

sanskrit: saṃnivārya ca yodhān svān satyena śapathena ca prāyojayad ameyātmā bhārgavāstraṃ mahābalaḥ
english: And having stayed his own warriors by a true oath, that mighty one of immeasurable soul brought to bear the Bhārgava weapon.

sanskrit: tato rājan sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca koṭiśaś ca śarās tīkṣṇā niragacchan mahāmṛdhe
english: Then, O king, sharp arrows by the thousands, the hundred-thousands, the hundred-millions, and the tens of millions poured forth in that great battle.

sanskrit: jvalitais tair mahāghoraiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ saṃchannā pāṇḍavī senā na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: Veiled by those blazing, most dreadful shafts winged with the feathers of heron and peacock, the Pāṇḍava army could no longer be discerned at all.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt pāñcālānāṃ viśāṃ pate pīḍitānāṃ balavatā bhārgavāstreṇa saṃyuge
english: A great cry of anguish arose among the Pāñcālas, O lord of peoples, tormented in the encounter by the mighty Bhārgava weapon.

sanskrit: nipatadbhir gajai rājan naraiś cāpi sahasraśaḥ rathaiś cāpi naravyāghra hayaiś cāpi samantataḥ
english: As elephants fell, O king, and men too by the thousands, and chariots and horses as well, O tiger among men, on every side,

sanskrit: prākampata mahī rājan nihatais tais tatas tataḥ vyākulaṃ sarvam abhavat pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam
english: the earth trembled, O king, beneath those slain on every side, and the whole great host of the Pāṇḍavas fell into utter confusion.
